_comment: Verbatim banner and panel copy, pinned to a version. This file is the evidence limb of consent_log.consent_text_version: the Git history is what shows WHAT the visitor read at the moment they consented (GDPR Art. 7(1)). NEVER EDIT THIS FILE IN PLACE — a copy change means a NEW version directory (2026-08-b, …), otherwise the evidence behind past decisions would change retroactively. A copy change is also a re-consent trigger (ICO: fresh consent is required when purposes/activities change).

banner.title: Cookies on this site
banner.body: We always use the cookies needed to run the site. Beyond that — only with your permission — we measure how visitors use the site, and we measure and personalise our Google and Meta advertising. Some of this data is transferred to the United States.
banner._button_rule: Accept and Reject are PIXEL-IDENTICAL in size, contrast, font and number of clicks. A unit test measures this, not a visual check — the compliance harness found this to be the fleet's most serious defect, and it is exactly what NAIH fined TV2 for (NAIH-3195/2022).

panel.title: Cookie settings
panel.intro: You can decide per category. You can change your decision at any time via the “Cookie settings” link at the bottom of the page.

necessary.label: Strictly necessary
necessary.body: Required for the site to work at all (security, forms, storing your cookie decision). We do not ask permission for these, because without them the site cannot be used.

analytics.label: Analytics
analytics.body: We measure how visitors use the site: which pages are popular, where people get stuck. Provider: Google (Google Analytics 4).

marketing.label: Marketing
marketing.body: Measuring and personalising our Google and Meta advertising. Providers: Google (Google Ads), Meta (Facebook, Instagram).

_copy_rules: FORBIDDEN: “if you reject, no data goes to any third party” — under advanced Consent Mode this is FALSE, and while any site in the fleet runs advanced it must not appear anywhere.
FORBIDDEN: “you won't get irrelevant ads” — not guaranteeable, therefore a promise rather than a fact.
REQUIRED: third parties BY NAME (Google, Meta) — vague “our partners” is expressly insufficient per both the ICO and NAIH.
REQUIRED: mention of the international (US) transfer.
Copy is factual and human, without promises.
